_comment: The hard-stop registry, machine-readable. The prose version lives in .claude/rules/autonomy.md and is the same six ids. This file exists because a forked subagent cannot ask a human anything: AskUserQuestion is stripped from every subagent in code, with no frontmatter escape. So each stop needs channels that work from where it fires. `preflight` patterns are matched against the phase's PLAN TEXT by the inline parent (skills/build), which asks before it forks. `inflight` patterns are matched against a Bash COMMAND by hooks/hard-stop.mjs, which returns permissionDecision:ask, because a permission prompt is the only channel that reaches a human from inside a fork. Anything that fires in neither is escalated by the worker as a HARD-STOP: line and asked by the parent. Every pattern is a JavaScript regex source, matched case-insensitively. Every stop carries fixtures and negative controls that `node hooks/hard-stop.mjs --selftest` runs, so a pattern that stops matching fails a test rather than failing silently in front of a user.

stops.title: Money movement or a payment
stops.why: Spends real funds. Never reversible by a retry.

preflight.question: This phase touches payments. Real money can move, and a payment is not reversible by re-running the phase. How should the build handle it?

options.label: Test mode
options.description: Build against test keys and test cards only. Nothing real moves. This is the default and the recommendation.

options.label: Stub it
options.description: Stub the payment path this phase and wire the real provider in a later, separate phase.

options.label: Live, I am here
options.description: Use live keys. Only pick this if you are watching the run and you accept a real charge.

preflight.fixture: Phase 4: wire the Stripe checkout session so a customer can pay for a seat.
mustNotMatch: Phase 2: add a pricing page with static copy that links to the sales form.

inflight.reason: This command runs against live payment credentials or creates a real charge. Money that moves is not returned by re-running the phase.

rules.name: create a charge, refund or subscription

stops.title: Accepting legal terms or a ToS
stops.why: Binds the user to an agreement they did not read.

preflight.question: This phase involves accepting terms on your behalf. An agent must not bind you to an agreement you have not read. Who accepts?

options.label: I will
options.description: Pause here. You read and accept the terms yourself, then the build carries on. This is the recommendation.

options.label: Already done
options.description: You have already accepted these terms. The build continues without pausing again.

options.label: Skip it
options.description: Drop the step that needs the agreement and record the gap in the plan.

preflight.fixture: Phase 1: accept the Apple Developer Program Licence Agreement so the app can be signed.
mustNotMatch: Phase 6: write the privacy policy page and link it from the footer.

inflight.reason: This command accepts an agreement on your behalf. An agent must not bind you to terms you have not read.

rules.name: agree to terms on the command line

stops.title: A destructive irreversible action
stops.why: Cannot be undone; a wrong call loses work permanently.

preflight.question: This phase contains a step that destroys data or rewrites history, and it cannot be undone by re-running the phase. How do you want it handled?

options.label: Back up first
options.description: Take a backup or a dump before the destructive step, then proceed. This is the recommendation.

options.label: Ask me again
options.description: Stop again at the exact moment the destructive command is about to run.

options.label: Skip it
options.description: Drop the destructive step from this phase and record it in the plan for a human to do.

preflight.fixture: Phase 3: drop the legacy sessions table once the new store is live.
mustMatch: Data migrations and rollback: irreversible, back up first.
This migration collapses duplicate rows and cannot be undone.
mustNotMatch: Phase 3: add a soft-delete flag to the posts table so nothing is removed.

inflight.reason: This command destroys work or rewrites history. It is not undone by re-running the phase.

stops.title: A production deploy
stops.why: Puts unverified change in front of real users.

preflight.question: This phase deploys to production, which puts unverified change in front of real users. How do you want it handled?

options.label: Preview only
options.description: Deploy to a preview or staging URL this phase. Production stays untouched until you say so. This is the recommendation.

options.label: Ask me again
options.description: Stop again at the exact moment the production deploy command is about to run.

options.label: Deploy live
options.description: Deploy to production in this run. Only pick this if you are watching.

preflight.fixture: Phase 6: deploy to production and point the domain at the new build.
mustNotMatch: Phase 5: push a preview deploy and check the Lighthouse score.

inflight.reason: This command deploys to production. Real users see the result immediately.

stops.title: Authenticating or provisioning an unbound provider
stops.why: Creates accounts, incurs cost, and grants access under the user's name.

preflight.question: This phase creates or authenticates an account with a third-party provider. That can cost money and grants access under your name. How do you want it handled?

options.label: Local only
options.description: Stay on local or free-tier infrastructure this phase, and provision the real thing later as its own step. This is the recommendation.

options.label: I will do it
options.description: Pause so you create the account yourself, then paste the keys in and the build carries on.

options.label: Go ahead
options.description: Create it during the run. You accept any cost and any terms it involves.

preflight.fixture: Phase 2: provision a Neon Postgres database and wire the connection string.
mustNotMatch: Phase 2: run Postgres locally in Docker and point DATABASE_URL at it.

inflight.reason: This command creates an account-level resource with a third-party provider, or signs you in to one. It can cost money and it grants access under your name.

rules.name: create a hosted project, database or bucket
rules.fixture: supabase projects create snip --org-id abc --region ap-southeast-2

stops.title: The final ship or merge
stops.why: The last gate before change is permanent and public.

preflight.question: This phase ships or merges, which is the last gate before the change is permanent and public. How do you want it handled?

options.label: Open a PR
options.description: Push the branch and open a pull request for you to review and merge yourself. This is the recommendation.

options.label: Ask me again
options.description: Stop again at the exact moment the ship or merge command is about to run.

options.label: Ship it
options.description: Complete the ship in this run. Only pick this if you are watching.

preflight.fixture: Phase 8: submit to the App Store and start the TestFlight rollout.
mustMatch: Phase 8: submit the iOS build to the App Store.
Phase 9: submit the final build to the App Store once the beta is signed off.
mustNotMatch: Phase 8: open a pull request and request review from the team.

inflight.reason: This command ships to a store or a public registry. It cannot be recalled once it is accepted.
